A 53-year-old male comes to his primary care doctor for a routine wellness visit. He reports feeling
generally well without specific concerns. His history reveals frequent alcohol consumption, high sodium
dietary intake, a sedentary lifestyle, and class I obesity. His vital signs show: temperature 98.6°F
(36.4°C), blood pressure 195/111 mmHg, pulse 75/min, respiratory rate 13/min, and oxygen saturation
99% on room air. Previous blood pressure readings from his last two visits were 159/100 mmHg and
162/99 mmHg. The physician plans to address his blood pressure management. Which intervention
would be most effective in treating this patient's hypertension? Answer Choices: (A) Alcohol cessation
(B) Calcium channel blocker monotherapy (C) Stress reduction techniques (D) ACE inhibitor initiation
(E) Regular aerobic exercise (F) Combination antihypertensive therapy (G) Sodium restriction (H)
Weight loss (I) Thiazide diuretic therapy (J) DASH diet
